name: Green Gables Inc
old_description: Green Gables Furniture is where rugged American craftsmanship meets undeniable style. Built in the USA from real solid wood, every piece is designed to feel substantial, authentic, and impossible to ignore. From bold reclaimed barnwood to rich live-edge hardwoods and refined contemporary designs, Green Gables creates furniture with character, presence, and the kind of quality that only gets better with time.
about:
Green Gables Furniture operates from Bradford, Illinois. The company traces its roots to the 1980s when a family-owned operation began building furniture out of a three-car garage. It remains proudly family owned today, with no outside ownership changes mentioned.

The firm manufactures solid wood furniture in the United States, working with reclaimed barnwood, live-edge hardwoods, and species such as Walnut, Cherry, Hickory, and White Oak. Production combines traditional woodworking techniques with contemporary design, incorporating steel accents and preserving natural character marks like knots, saw marks, and grain variation. The company notes that these features are not imperfections but what make each piece one of a kind. Specific facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not disclosed.

End customers purchase pieces for home use, ranging from rustic Western styles to clean, modern collections such as the Silverton and Steelbound lines.

The company emphasizes distinctive design, authentic materials, and craftsmanship that can be seen and felt. Its stated goal is to build beautiful, honest furniture with real character — pieces that don’t simply fill a room but become part of it — and to build them well enough to be enjoyed for generations.

The installation team includes a chief troubleshooter and two solar technicians alongside the owner and sales manager.

Green Leaf Solar emphasizes risk reduction for customers by handling incentive paperwork and offering long-term warranties. Owner Ryan Roe applies a mathematics background to system design for cost effectiveness, while Sales Manager Jay Hasheider brings over three decades of utility experience from Columbia Water and Light, including state recognition for resource stewardship.

name: Green Mountain Semiconductor, Inc.
old_description: GMS specializes in Custom Analog, Digital & Mixed Signal design.
about:
Green Mountain Semiconductor, Inc. was founded in 2015 in Burlington, Vermont, by three friends and colleagues who began collaborating on semiconductor design projects. The company remains headquartered in Burlington, where its engineering team performs all design work in-house.

The firm provides custom analog, digital, and mixed-signal ASIC design services, with deep expertise in memory design (DRAM, SRAM, emerging non-volatile memory) and compute-in-memory architectures. Its service offerings include AI circuit design, emerging memory development, special-purpose applications, and high-speed interface solutions such as LPDDR4/4X/5 and SPI/QPI PHYs. The team has experience in advanced process nodes, including 7 nm TSMC, and holds seven patents in commodity memory architecture, error correction, and in-memory high-parallel data processing.

Green Mountain Semiconductor serves aerospace and defense, high-performance computing, and medical device markets. In aerospace and defense, it develops radiation-hardened neuromorphic processors for NASA and works on SWaP-optimized sensor-processing chips. For medical devices, it creates low-power integrated circuits for patient monitoring and diagnosis, including neuromorphic edge-computing IP. The company also supports high-performance computing platforms with custom memory and interface IP.

The company emphasizes its 100% U.S.-based design team, with all work performed by employees at its Burlington offices. Its differentiation rests on a combination of memory-design heritage, patented in-memory computing techniques, and a focus on size, weight, and power (SWaP) optimization for demanding applications.

about:
Green Muscle Solar operates from Sun City, Arizona. The company was founded by co-owners Jim, Brent, Paula, and Jamell on the principle of treating customers right and putting their interests first. Leadership team members each bring over 11 years of hands-on solar experience, honed while working with the nation’s largest solar installer.

The firm provides solar installation, consulting, and service & maintenance for residential systems. Installation projects are overseen by a dedicated Project Manager rather than a commissioned sales representative, and Master Electricians supervise every install to ensure code compliance. Crews handle roof penetration sealing, conduit runs, wiring, and main-panel tie-ins. The service division troubleshoots production issues, performs preventative maintenance, and services out-of-warranty systems.

Green Muscle serves homeowners who have existing solar contracts, offering detailed production analysis, contract review, and system inspections. Its maintenance work targets previously installed systems that are out of warranty, correcting installation defects that affect output. Referrals from satisfied residential customers drive much of the business.

The company differentiates itself through an integrity-and-education approach, emphasizing real value over sales pressure. Rigorous installer training, direct project management, and a referral-based model reflect its founding belief that customer care builds lasting trust.

about:
Greene Textile Inc operates from Montebello, California, in the heart of Southern California's textile corridor. The company was founded in 2001 by two brothers who had relocated from New York to California in the 1980s, joining a family network already established in the local textile trade. After two decades of working with yarn suppliers, knitting mills, and dye houses, the brothers launched their own venture from a small office above a knitting mill before expanding to their current Telegraph Road facility, which now houses a showroom, warehouse, and operations.

The firm specializes in knit-to-order production, maintaining a library of more than 4,000 fabric styles primarily in cotton. Its capabilities span yarn sourcing, custom knitting, and both piece and garment dyeing, allowing clients to develop unique colorways and finishes. The Montebello facility supports full vertical integration from yarn selection through finished fabric, and the company also carries an inventory of in-stock fabrics for immediate shipment.

Greene Textile serves clothing brands and small businesses across the apparel sector, providing custom-developed knits for fashion labels as well as low-minimum-order stock fabrics for emerging designers and garment-dye houses. Its customer base includes brands seeking domestic production with flexible volume requirements.

The company emphasizes a family-oriented approach to manufacturing, citing the principle that treating every partner like family underpins its operational philosophy. This culture, rooted in the founders' early experience within the Southern California textile community, is presented as the foundation of its reliability and responsiveness.

old_description: At Gulf Side Fabricators, our certifications and capabilities reflect our commitment to excellence across every facet of custom fabrication:
about:
Gulf Side Fabricators, LLC, was founded in October 2010 in Broussard, Louisiana, by industry veterans with over two decades of hands-on experience. The founders, having seen the market settle for "good enough," set out to raise the bar for custom metal fabrication on the Gulf Coast.

The company operates a 24,000-square-foot campus that includes separate facilities for carbon steel and exotic alloys such as stainless steel, super duplex, copper nickel, and aluminum. Its core processes cover FCAW, GMAW, SMAW, and GTAW welding, ASME-coded pressure vessel fabrication (U and R stamps), B31.3 process piping, and DNV 2.7-1/2.7-3 offshore container manufacturing. In-house hydrostatic testing and advanced nesting software that reduces material waste by up to 30% support the workflow.

The shop's certifications allow it to meet the stringent documentation and testing requirements of these regulated sectors.

The firm emphasizes "Innovation Over Imitation" and "Excellence Without Exception," investing in technology and training rather than shortcuts. Its Louisiana roots are framed as a strategic advantage, providing deep regional industry connections and a workforce committed to the area's industrial future.

The molder serves as both a Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier to a range of industries, with a documented relationship with GE Appliance, which recognized HB Molding with a 2017 Supplier Quality Performance Award and a 2018 Silent Warrior award. Most customers are within a 200-mile radius of Louisville.

Hallam attributes the company's growth to its ability to react quickly to customer needs and opportunities. The quality team establishes control plans to match or exceed project requirements, emphasizing on-time delivery and attention to detail.

Experience a fusion of innovative techniques and timeless craftsmanship, tailored to transform your visions into reality.
about:
HG Metals, a structural and miscellaneous steel fabrication company, operates from Indianapolis, Indiana. It functions as an active division of HGMC Supply, Inc., with Ashley Collins serving as president and owner. The business was established over two decades ago to provide steel solutions for commercial and construction projects across Indiana and the United States.

The company fabricates structural steel framing, support systems, custom stairs, rails, ladders, mezzanines, equipment platforms, canopies, and specialty metal items. Its Indianapolis facility is equipped with modern CNC machinery and staffed by AWS D1.1‑certified welders. HG Metals maintains membership in the American Institute of Steel Construction (AISC) and adheres to NAAMM and NOMMA guidelines, producing all work in‑house and shipping nationwide.

Primary customers are general contractors, developers, and commercial construction firms. Recent projects include structural steel packages for large‑scale commercial developments and one‑of‑a‑kind custom fabrications for specialty builds. The firm serves clients throughout Indiana and across the United States.

HG Metals emphasizes clear communication, dependable scheduling, and accountability from bid through final delivery. Leadership states that their differentiation lies in building relationships, solving problems, and keeping steel on the critical path of each project.

name: HMB Electronics
old_description: We stock brand new and authentic IC’s from the industry’s leading manufacturers such as Analog Devices, TI, Intel, Xilinx, Maxim, and more. In a rush? We offer expedited shipping to get them to you the next day!
about:
HMB Electronics, a women-owned small business, is headquartered in North Haven, Connecticut, where it services the Northeast region of the United States. The company was established to meet growing demand for expedited shipments and regional service by leveraging a vast network of electronic component suppliers both domestically and internationally.

As a stocking distributor, HMB Electronics carries name-brand electronic components — including integrated circuits, resistors, transistors, capacitors, connectors, and computer peripherals — from manufacturers such as Analog Devices, Texas Instruments, Intel, Xilinx, and Maxim. It offers same-day shipping on stocked items and next-day expedited delivery. For hard-to-find or end-of-life parts, the company sources through domestic and international channels, purchases excess inventory from reputable suppliers, and provides cross-referencing support. Component authenticity is verified via a partner testing facility on the East Coast, and manufacturer traceability certificates are supplied when available. Inventory is held in a climate-controlled, anti-static warehouse with continuous monitoring.

The distributor serves government agencies, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), contract manufacturers (CMs), and both franchised and non-franchised distributors. Its customer base spans the military, information technology, and OEM sectors, with the company noting it works with industry leaders in those fields.

HMB Electronics emphasizes rapid fulfillment, traceability, and quality assurance as key differentiators. It maintains AS5553 compliance for counterfeit electronic parts avoidance, detection, mitigation, and disposition, and aims to guarantee authentic components with manufacturer traceability wherever possible.

name: Haake Manufacturing Co
old_description: We’re not just sheet metal fabricators. We’re professional problem solvers ready to help solve your complex metal part challenges.
about:
Haake Manufacturing Co. operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility in De Soto, Missouri. The company was founded in 1948 by Fred C. Haake Sr., a German-trained machinist, and his wife Elfriede, who opened a small tool-and-die shop in their St. Louis garage with a single punch press. In 1963, the second generation — Fred Jr. and Lorraine Haake — relocated the business to De Soto and added a dedicated trucking operation to control delivery. Today the company is led by fourth-generation family member Jay Rieker, maintaining continuous family ownership since inception.

The shop provides full-service precision sheet metal fabrication under one roof. Core processes include CNC laser cutting (up to 10,000 watts), CNC punching with 360-degree tool rotation, combined punch/laser cells that form and contour in a single setup, CNC press brake forming with six-axis back gauges, metal stamping on AIDA cells up to 160 tons (supplemented by 5–150-ton presses), robotic MIG/MAG welding of steel, stainless steel, and aluminum, and a fully automated powder coating line with six-stage wash, infrared pre-processing, and zirconium pretreatment. Secondary services cover assembly, hardware insertion, and finish coordination.

Haake serves manufacturers across the United States, with historical roots in the St. Louis industrial base. The company now supports reshoring programs and just-in-time inventory strategies for OEMs and contract assemblers requiring domestic supply-chain stability.

The founding principle — deliver parts that arrive on time and fit flawlessly — remains the stated differentiator. Haake emphasizes its central U.S. location, in-house freight, and solar-assisted low operating costs as structural advantages that enable 2-day shipping to either coast, 99% on-time delivery, and defect rates of 292 PPM for fabrication and 0 PPM for powder coating (2025 data).

old_description: HaF Equipment is a dry ingredient handling equipment manufacturer whose systems are designed to focus on partner success and excellence across various verticals and applications, from the food industry to pharmaceuticals and plastics.
about:
Haf Equipment, based in Maplewood, Minnesota, was launched in 1994 by founder Pete Hoefler with a focus on dry material handling. The company remains USA-based and serves businesses worldwide.

The company designs and manufactures custom material handling equipment and systems, including filter receivers, bulk bag unloaders, feeders, pneumatic and mechanical conveyors, blending equipment, dust collection, dry sorbent injection, air pollution control, batching systems, and liquid handling assemblies. It offers system integration, batching, unloading, packaging, controls, and multiple conveying phases. Two product lines serve different needs: the H-Series provides pre-engineered, off-the-shelf equipment for faster delivery, while the M-Series features tool-free, quick take-apart designs customized to specific applications.

Haf serves industries such as food processing (dairy, bakery, snacks, pet food, nutraceuticals), plastics, rubber, chemical, pharmaceuticals, ceramics, steel, air pollution control, and batteries.

The company differentiates itself through operator-centric designs and a quality control process that inspects every piece of equipment before shipment. Its "HAF Difference" values emphasize team focus, humble confidence, elite performance, hustle, and driven-yet-fun culture. In 2024, Haf acquired the assets of Semi Bulk Systems to expand its product lines into both dry and liquid ingredient handling.

name: Hampshire Controls Corporation
old_description: Established in 1976 and based in Dover, New Hampshire, Hampshire Controls is a leading designer and manufacturer of supremely reliable “Made in the USA” monitoring, logging, and alert status notification systems for demanding applications.
about:
Hampshire Controls Corporation was established in 1976 in Dover, New Hampshire. The company designs and manufactures monitoring, data logging, and alarm notification systems for demanding applications, emphasizing "Made in the USA" reliability.

The product line includes NIST-traceable temperature monitors and alarms (configurable with 2 to 8 channels), cryogenic temperature monitors, multi-probe condition monitors, the T° Sentry ALERT data logging and alarm system, Wi-Fi temperature transmitters, biomedical freezer backup systems (liquid CO2 and liquid nitrogen), LN2 level monitors, laboratory air flow monitors, and remote alarm delay modules. Manufacturing services encompass PCB soldering, cable manufacturing, subsystem interfacing, final electronic assembly, electronic testing, burn-in, and NIST-traceable calibration, all performed at the Dover facility. The firm also provides custom mechanical and electrical engineering, firmware development, and communication protocol implementation (BACnet, Modbus, MQTT, HTTP/HTTPS, etc.).

Hampshire Controls serves blood banks, cryogenic biologic storage facilities, vaccine and genetic research laboratories, biopharma production plants, governmental agencies, hospitals, commercial food processing and storage operations, and industrial manufacturers. It also supplies original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) with high-volume temperature monitoring and alarm systems for clinical, food and beverage, water distribution, plumbing, and industrial markets.

The company differentiates itself through in-house design, manufacturing, and calibration capabilities, allowing it to offer both standard and custom-engineered products with NIST-traceable calibration. Its systems are UL LISTED and built to meet NEMA/IP ratings for harsh environments.

name: Hanley's Foods
old_description: Hanley’s makes premium, natural salad dressings with a taste of Louisiana.
about:
Hanley's Foods is based in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. The company was founded in 2010 by Richard and Kate Hanley, a couple who have been together since high school. The business originated in 2012 when the pair discovered their favorite restaurant-style dressing, Sensation®, was unavailable in stores. After testing recipes at salad parties with family and friends, they launched the winning formula at the Red Stick Farmers Market, where it sold out repeatedly. They later partnered with the LSU AgCenter's Food Incubator to scale production.

The company manufactures premium salad dressings and croutons, producing every bottle from scratch in its Louisiana facility. Hanley's focuses exclusively on these two product lines, using natural, locally sourced ingredients. Its products are now stocked in more than 2,000 retail locations across the United States.

Hanley's serves the retail grocery and foodservice sectors. Its customer base includes national chains such as Walmart, Costco, Whole Foods Market, and Winn-Dixie, as well as regional grocers like Rouses Markets and AG Stores. The company also supplies foodservice operators including Compass Group and Royal Caribbean.

The founders started Hanley's to bring a beloved local dressing to the broader market. The company emphasizes a single-minded commitment to quality, citing certifications such as HACCP, NSF, SQF, and GMP, and a philosophy of using premium, natural ingredients sourced from south Louisiana.

name: Hansen Plastics Corporation
old_description: Hansen Plastics Corporation: Plastic Manufacturers in Illinois & Custom Injection Molding Services
about:
Hansen Plastics Corporation operates from Elgin, Illinois, where it was founded in 1971 by Elmer Hansen. The company transitioned to an Employee Stock Ownership Plan in 1991 and became fully employee-owned by 1998, a structure that remains central to its culture and decision-making.

The shop runs more than 70 injection molding presses ranging from 28 to 500 tons across over 150,000 square feet of production space. Core processes include horizontal, vertical/insert, and multi-material molding, supported by decoupled molding and RJG scientific molding with cavity-pressure transducers. Value-added operations cover in-mold decorating, hot stamping, pad printing, machining, ultrasonic welding, thermal insertion, assembly, and custom packaging.

Hansen serves OEMs and manufacturers across North America in automotive, life safety, appliances, fluid movement and water treatment, transportation (non-automotive), construction, and agriculture. Long-term customers include Elkay in water delivery and Motive Products in automotive tools.

The company traces its differentiation to its employee-owner model and a founding motto of "do it right the first time." Its quality system is built on ISO 9001:2015 with statistical process control looped into business systems, aiming for zero defects through data-driven process control and lean manufacturing practices.

about:
Haven Steel Products began building its first production facility in Haven, Kansas, in 1968 and started producing spring steel components the following year. The privately owned company was founded as a fabricator for the agricultural, construction, and trailer industries, and the original 7,000‑square‑foot building has since grown to more than 200,000 square feet of production space across two plants in Haven, Kansas, and McKenzie, Tennessee.

The company forges, hot‑forms, heat‑treats, powder‑coats, laser‑cuts, and builds tooling in‑house. Its Kansas plant runs eight quench‑and‑temper lines, a 30 kW Bodor fiber laser with bevel capability on carbon steel up to 2 inches thick, and a new Flex CNC cell; the Tennessee plant recently added two 700‑ton forging presses, a 36‑inch belt furnace, and a slurry‑coating line for Ultra Tuf Coatings™. Together the sites operate multiple natural‑gas furnaces, induction heaters, and a growing fleet of Kuka robots.

Haven Steel supplies heat‑treated and tempered components to major OEMs and short‑line manufacturers in agriculture (tillage sweeps, disc blades, rotary cutter blades), construction (landscaping and mowing parts), trailer production (leaf springs, seat springs, weight‑equalizing hitch springs), railroad (wear plates), recycling (chopper knives), grounds maintenance (aerator knives), playground equipment, and patio furniture.

The company emphasizes full traceability—every shipped part can be traced back to its raw‑steel heat and process history—and maintains an ISO 9001:2015 quality system with third‑party calibrated inspection equipment and a minimum three‑year documentation retention. Recent investments in automation, additional furnace capacity, and the proprietary Ultra Tuf Coatings™ line reflect a focus on extending component wear life three to five times over standard parts.

Customers are typically companies building hardware where die placement within microns, thermal cycling survival, and first-lot qualification are critical.

The company differentiates itself with a data-driven, AI-native approach: designed experiments (DOE) replace trial-and-error, statistical process control and aggregated build data drive decisions, and AI surfaces drift and correlations to reduce iterations. All development and build work remains on US soil with a domestic supply chain, and detailed design rules and process data are shared under NDA.

name: High-Purity Silicon America Corporation
old_description: In a field driven by the demand for quality - where purity is measured in "parts per trillion" - HSA has established itself as an industry leader. With a relentless pursuit of the highest level of excellence in every phase of corporate growth and development, HSA is committed to the "never-ending process" - the Continuum of Quality. We strive to understand and meet the needs of our employees, customers and neighbors. We continually look for ways to improve our processes, procedures, people, and products; because we realize that quality is a never-ending process. We strive to become the industry's preferred supplier of Polysilicon by satisfying our customer's needs for product performance, technical service and on-time delivery.
about:
High-Purity Silicon America Corporation (HSA) operates from Theodore, Alabama. The company was incorporated in 1996 as Mitsubishi Polycrystalline America Corporation, a wholly owned subsidiary of Mitsubishi Materials Corporation (MMC).

HSA manufactures polycrystalline silicon (polysilicon) in reduction furnaces at its Theodore facility. The plant also yields semiconductor-grade by-products — silicon tetrachloride and trichlorosilane — that serve as raw materials for epitaxial semiconductors and fiber-optic cables. Quality control relies on ultra-micro analysis equipment: floating-zone (Fz) conversion to single-crystal silicon for electrical-property measurement, photoluminescence (PL) for dopant detection down to parts-per-trillion levels, and ICP mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS) for metallic impurity screening. Additional analytical capabilities include gas chromatography (GC), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and ICP atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES).

The company supplies polysilicon and saline by-products to the semiconductor and fiber-optic industries. Its materials feed epitaxial wafer production and optical-cable manufacturing, where purity measured in parts per trillion is a prerequisite.

HSA describes its guiding philosophy as a "Continuum of Quality" — a never-ending process of improving processes, procedures, people, and products to become the industry's preferred polysilicon supplier through product performance, technical service, and on-time delivery.

The company began by building custom cabinets and furniture from solid wood, using wood joinery instead of screws and nails and applying four coats of finish where three were typical. It also specialized in antique furniture restoration and repair from the start.

Today the shop operates from a 2,400-square-foot facility where it builds bookcases, entertainment centers, bath and kitchen cabinets, and other solid-wood furniture. All pieces feature inset, flush doors and drawers in traditional styles such as Mission, Shaker, and beaded face frames. Drawers are dovetailed for strength, and every surface receives four coats of finish inside and out. Restoration work is done by hand: old finishes are stripped manually rather than dipped, joints are repaired, and stains are color-matched to original pieces.

Projects range from new traditional-style kitchen cabinets to the repair of family antiques intended for another 80 years of service.

Hinrichs Fine Woods differentiates itself through its commitment to hand-crafted joinery, hand-applied finishes, and restoration methods that preserve the integrity of original pieces. The founder's original quality standards—extra finish coats, wood joints over mechanical fasteners, and meticulous hand stripping—remain the benchmark for every project.

old_description: We source and supply new, obsolete, and hard-to-find board-level electronic components — all independently tested at ISO/IEC 17025-accredited labs. Every order is certified, compliant, and backed by our 90-day quality guarantee.
about:
Based in Tampa, Florida, Honest Components, Inc. operates as a woman-owned small business (WOSB) certified by the U.S. Small Business Administration. The company was built by a team with over 50 combined years of experience in electronic hardware and software, led by President Jackie Schwab, who brings more than 30 years of sales leadership and customer advocacy.

Honest Components specializes in sourcing and supplying new, obsolete, and hard-to-find board-level electronic components. Its line card includes over 50,000 part numbers from manufacturers such as AMD, Intel, and Texas Instruments, covering connectors, capacitors, microcontrollers, and memory chips. Every order undergoes third-party authentication at independent laboratories accredited to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 and AS6171, including visual inspection, X-ray imaging, decapsulation, solderability, and functional testing. The company manages the full procurement lifecycle — from vendor qualification and order management to logistics — and has supplied more than 200,000 authenticated components to date.

The distributor serves aerospace, defense, medical, and industrial customers, including OEMs and contract manufacturers with mission-critical requirements. It is ITAR registered and a member of the Government-Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP) to combat counterfeit parts, making it a qualified supplier for U.S. defense-related programs. Healthcare and medical equipment manufacturers also rely on its certified components for regulated applications.

Honest Components differentiates itself by bearing the cost of independent third-party testing on every order at no charge to the customer, backing each shipment with a 90-day form, fit, and function guarantee. Its WOSB certification supports supplier diversity goals, while its AS9120B and ISO 9001:2015 quality management system ensures traceability and compliance across the supply chain.

old_description: Our Sweet Pepper Relish is made with the plumpest, sweetest red bell peppers, while our Hot Pepper relish is made with red bell peppers and green peppers. Or try our Classic Green Tomato Piccalilli with the sweet and savory taste like your great grandmother used to make, made of green tomatoes, red peppers, onions, brown sugar, cider vinegar and a secret blend of spices.​
about:
Howard Foods Inc. is headquartered in Danvers, Massachusetts. The company traces its origins to the early 1890s when John F. Howard and his wife Margaret began producing relishes in the kitchen of their Bradford hotel. The business was incorporated in 1924 after Howard sold it to Arthur D. Dickson, and merged with the C.E. Chapin Company in 1926. Since 1990, the company has been under its current ownership, with the sales office relocated to Danvers.

Howard Foods manufactures a line of gourmet condiments that includes Sweet Pepper Relish, Hot Pepper Relish, Green Tomato Piccalilli, Ham Glaze, Garlic Seasoning Juice, and Onion Seasoning Juice. The products are made using traditional recipes that the company says have not changed since the 19th century. The firm also offers pure maple syrup. No details on facility size, headcount, or annual volume are disclosed.

The company serves retail grocery stores throughout New England, foodservice operators such as restaurants, and direct-to-consumer customers through its online store. Its relishes have been used by generations of families and restaurants, and the Sweet Pepper Relish is described as the bestselling sweet pepper relish in the United States.

Howard Foods emphasizes natural ingredients, simplicity, and recipes that have withstood the test of time. Its products earned a Grand Prix at the 1900 International Exhibition in Paris for purity and quality, and the company promotes its relishes as delivering great flavor at value prices without sacrificing quality.

Huetter Mill & Cabinet operates from Murray, Utah, where it was founded in 1948 by Alfred Huetter, a German immigrant who began building window sash and custom millwork in a chicken coop behind his family home in the 1930s. The business remains family-owned, now led by President Gordon Huetter, Alfred’s son.

The company manufactures custom millwork, stair parts, handrails, and hardwood moldings from a dedicated production facility and showroom in Murray. It stocks moldings in alder, knotty alder, maple, poplar, cherry, and oak, maintains a library of custom knives for unique profiles, and produces curved stairways and complete stair systems. Inventory exceeds $1.2 million, and the firm uses advanced machinery staffed by skilled craftsmen to serve both commercial and high-end residential projects, shipping nationally.

Huetter Mill serves commercial construction, residential new builds, and remodeling markets, with a specialty in historic restoration. Past projects include the Utah Governor’s Mansion, Utah State Capitol, The Children’s Center, and O.C. Tanner renovations. Capabilities extend to schools, hospitals, tenant improvements, court buildings, and correctional facilities.

The company’s stated purpose is to provide a financially sound source for wholesale millwork and commercial shop products at reasonable cost, delivered efficiently by trained employees. Its motto, “Quality and Craftsmanship live in our Name,” reflects the multi-generational commitment to that standard.

Imricor’s customers are hospitals and medical centers building interventional MR labs for cardiac ablation. The company also maintains strategic collaborations with Philips and GE HealthCare to integrate its technology into broader MR imaging platforms.

about:
Innovative Plastek Solutions was founded in 2012 in Loretto, Tennessee, near the Shoals region of northern Alabama. The company began as a urethane molder producing decorative furniture parts for southern manufacturers that lacked local plastic décor suppliers.

The operation has since expanded into thermoplastic injection molding, with machines capable of 270-ton clamping force, 21.2-ounce shot size, and 32-inch maximum part length. Services include overmolding, secondary finishing, vacuum metalizing, insert molding, 3D-printed samples, short-run production, and conversion of urethane parts to injection-molded components. The facility also provides value-added assembly, kitting, JIT warehousing, tooling storage, and a dedicated freight fleet of box trucks and vans.

The company serves the furniture, automotive, consumer-products, aerospace, healthcare, and military sectors. Examples cited include promotional furniture hardware, auto parts, child seats, precision military components, and medical device parts. It ships throughout North America and Canada.

The founders identified a regional gap—southern furniture makers had no nearby source for plastic decorative parts—and built the business to offer lower costs than large northern molders by transitioning urethane castings to injection molding.

Innovative Sensor Technology (IST) USA Division operates from Las Vegas, Nevada, established in 2001 as the American sales and support arm of the Swiss sensor manufacturer IST AG. The U.S. office provides local supply-chain programs and technical support from on-site stock.

IST develops and manufactures a broad portfolio of physical, chemical, and biological sensors, including temperature sensors (thin-film platinum RTDs), thermal mass flow sensors, humidity sensors, conductivity sensors, biosensors, micro heaters, and thermal infrared emitters. Production occurs at the headquarters in Switzerland and a dedicated facility in Rožnov pod Radhoštěm, Czech Republic, with the group employing roughly 500 people worldwide. The company offers standard sensors through an online shop for small lots and handles custom adaptations up to full co-development of new sensor technologies, producing around 200 new sensor variants annually.

IST sensors serve medical technology, process automation, electric vehicles, aerospace (including ESCC-qualified space flight models), test and measurement, biotechnology, food and beverage conductivity monitoring, oil-condition monitoring, and emission-monitoring systems. Customers range from instrument OEMs and research institutes to high-reliability aerospace primes.

The company emphasizes Swiss engineering precision, end-to-end development support from concept through after-sales service, flexible order quantities with short lead times, and a partnership model that includes collaboration with universities and research institutes. Its quality and environmental management systems are certified to ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 14001:2015.

about:
Integrated Semiconductor Solutions (ISS) is based in Santa Ana, California. The company was founded in 2001 by Troy Gray, who serves as CEO. Since 2010, ISS has operated as a dedicated partner to integrated circuit manufacturers, offering a full suite of semiconductor reliability qualification and testing services.

ISS specializes in stress-based reliability testing, including process reliability stress testing, package qualification, and both qualification and production-level burn-in services. The lab also performs ESD testing (HBM, MM, CDM) and latch-up testing to JEDEC and ESDA standards. In addition to testing, the company designs, fabricates, and assembles custom printed circuit boards for burn-in, ESD/latch-up, and automatic test equipment (ATE) applications. Equipment includes a Model Oryx CDM 9000 system for charged-device-model testing and multiple Criteria XXV C25 burn-in ovens, each with six zones and 48 slots, providing capacity for high-volume production runs.

The primary customers are fabless semiconductor companies and start-up integrated device manufacturers (IDMs) that require independent qualification of their IC designs. ISS also works with established IC manufacturers needing package qualification and production burn-in support. The company's AS9100D certification indicates capability for aerospace and defense-related programs, though the core client base remains commercial semiconductor firms.

ISS emphasizes a single-source model that combines engineering expertise with in-house board fabrication to reduce lead times and control quality.

Intronics serves eight core markets: Computers & Communication, Aerospace & Defense, Electric Power Utility, Industrial Automation, Transportation, Medical Device, Space Systems, and Emerging Technologies such as AI hardware and quantum computing. Its components have been used in satellite designs, medical imaging equipment, and industrial power converters for automotive manufacturing plants, as noted by a chief engineer at an aerospace firm, an R&D director at a medical device company, and a plant manager at an automotive manufacturer.

The company emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015‑certified manufacturing, MIL‑STD‑compliant designs for defense programs, and radiation‑hardened electronics for space applications. It positions its differentiation on combining innovative design with rigorous testing to meet demanding requirements across multiple industries.

The team also relies on seasoned hand craftsmanship for joinery and finishing, allowing both precision and custom detail.

The firm emphasizes continuous learning, adopting new software and building methods while retaining the hands-on approach that began with a handsaw and scrap lumber.

The operation also curates a line of artisanal pantry goods, home fragrances, and gift sets sourced from regional makers.

Products are sold directly to consumers through an online mercantile and offered wholesale to retailers and specialty food shops.

The revival was driven by a desire to preserve Appalachian salt-making heritage and showcase the mineral-rich character of the local brine. The founders emphasize small-batch craftsmanship and partnerships with artisans who share their commitment to authenticity.

The team of 24 employees ships roughly 50,000 custom parts per month from their North Little Rock facility, with a second location opened in spring 2025 and a Texas site planned.

JAMM serves architecture and construction firms (structural components, railings), manufacturers and industrial clients (conveyor parts, assembled configurations), and individuals and businesses seeking custom specialty items such as sculptures, fixtures, and signage. Customers include Heating and Cooling Systems of Arkansas, which uses them for commercial projects.

The founders started the company to fill a gap in well-built custom handrails for train cars, and their mission emphasizes aligning experience, capabilities, and technology to build customers' dreams while fostering a supportive environment for their team. They highlight free quotes, in-house certified welding, and a single-source approach from design through finishing.

about:
JEM Electronics, Inc. was founded in 1981 by John McDonald in Franklin, Massachusetts.

Today JEM operates from its headquarters in Franklin, MA, and a production facility in Tijuana, Mexico, providing build-to-print manufacturing from prototype through high-volume production. Core capabilities include custom cable assembly, complex wire harness assembly, and integrated box-build electromechanical assembly. Every assembly undergoes 100% in-house testing—continuity, pull, hipot, and VSWR—under documented procedures aligned with IPC/WHMA-A-620 workmanship standards. The company employs cross-trained assemblers and applies Lean Six Sigma methods to maintain process consistency.

JEM serves OEMs in regulated, high-reliability sectors including military and defense, medical, semiconductor, robotics, renewable energy, oil and gas, and networking. Its ITAR registration and CAGE code 3DTF7 support defense and government contract work, while ISO 9001:2015 and UL/CSA certifications cover commercial and industrial requirements.

The company differentiates itself by reviewing every drawing for manufacturability before quoting, delivering transparent timelines, and standing behind each assembly with full traceability documentation. McDonald’s original vision—to solve customer problems through modern technology and repeatable quality—remains the guiding principle behind JEM’s disciplined, documented process from drawing to delivery.

about:
JUNE Medical USA Inc is based in New Castle, Delaware, serving as the U.S. entity of JUNE Medical, a privately owned medical device group with offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, and Sweden. The company manages early-stage innovation, research and development, manufacturing, and global commercialization through its sister company Mosaic Surgical, which acts as the manufacturing arm. The name "JUNE" began as a secret code name before launch, chosen to represent spring, growth, and the future; no founding year or individual founders are disclosed in public materials.

The product portfolio centers on surgical devices designed to simplify procedures and reduce reliance on manual assistance. Flagship products include the Galaxy II self-retaining surgical retractor, the HandMe retractor for hand surgery, the LUX Connect flexible surgical light, Oxiplex adhesion barriers for intrauterine or peritoneal surgery, and the Thermablate EAS portable balloon system for heavy menstrual bleeding. Primary customers are healthcare providers, including the U.K. National Health Service (NHS) and private hospital groups such as Circle Health Group, Nuffield Health, and Ramsay Healthcare. The Swedish subsidiary, JUNE Medical Sverige AB, handles direct sales to Swedish healthcare and serves as the EU Authorized Representative for the group. Mosaic Surgical additionally offers U.K. Responsible Person services for other manufacturers seeking to place medical devices on the U.K. market.

The company states its purpose as improving access to medical devices, building partnerships for safer surgery, and reducing the environmental impact of surgery. Differentiators highlighted include the HandMe retractor eliminating the need for an extra pair of hands during operations, the Galaxy II retractor lowering cost and environmental footprint while replacing an assistant, and the LUX Connect light offering unlimited positioning flexibility. The quality policy, authorized by CEO Angela Spang, emphasizes customer focus, continual improvement, and evidence-based decision making.

The company remanufactures transformers, voltage regulators, and switchgear, and provides repair, testing, and diagnostic services for oil-filled electrical equipment. Transformer offerings range from single-phase pole-mount units (5–500 kVA) to three-phase substation and pad-mount units up to 10 MVA. The company emphasizes fast, affordable solutions without sacrificing quality, backing remanufactured transformers with a three-year warranty. Its differentiation rests on using new rather than filtered oil, new copper conductors, and a reclamation process designed to minimize environmental impact while maximizing material recovery.

about:
Jones Plastic & Engineering was founded in 1961 in Louisville, Kentucky, by Harry and Larry Jones as a single-machine operation producing whiskey bottle caps. The family-owned business, now headed by the second and third generations of the Jones family, is based in Jeffersontown, Kentucky, and operates nine facilities across the United States and Mexico.

The company provides integrated plastic manufacturing services, including product development, tooling, injection molding (65 to 3,150 tons across five facilities), robotic paint, hydrographics, assembly, and testing. A dedicated 90,000-square-foot paint and hydrographics plant in Juárez, Mexico, houses a 25,000-square-foot clean-room paint line with FANUC robots, RFID-controlled rack systems, and a 1.3-meter hydrographic dip tank. An in-house 3D printing lab runs FDM and PolyJet systems for functional prototypes and short-run injection molded samples. Total manufacturing space approaches 1.6 million square feet with roughly 3,000 employees.

Jones Plastic serves automotive, appliance, powersports, outdoor products, consumer goods, and industrial and defense markets, supplying components and assemblies to North American OEMs. The company also operates Rev-A-Shelf, a wholly owned subsidiary that manufactures residential cabinet storage and organizational products.

The firm pioneered gas-assist injection molding in the early 1990s and emphasizes an engineering-first approach, using solid modeling, CAE simulation, and rapid prototyping to validate designs before tooling. Integrating molding, finishing, and assembly under one supply chain aims to reduce freight, handling, and coordination costs. Quality management is ISO 9001 certified.

about:
Kelley Bean Co. traces its roots to 1927 when the Chester B. Brown Company was founded in Morrill, Nebraska, with Robert L. Kelley Sr. as plant manager. In 1969, Robert L. Kelley Sr. and his son Gary L. Kelley established Kelley Bean Co. in Henry, Nebraska.

The company originates, processes, and markets dry edible beans — including Pinto, Great Northern, and numerous other varieties — sourced from a network of grower partnerships across the High Plains. Processing facilities run a "triple clean" line: screen sizing, gravity separation (including de-stoners), and optical electric-eye sorting, supplemented by rare-earth magnets, metal detection, and pre-wash equipment. Kelley Bean operates multiple GFSI-certified plants and maintains its own P.A.S.S. (Process Assuring Safety and Specification) food-safety system. Klann Plastics operates from Waynesboro, Virginia, where it was founded in 1910 by August Klann as a builder of pipe organs. As a fully custom injection molder with no proprietary products, Klann provides plastic injection molding, insert and over-molding, medical clean room molding in Class 10,000 environments, mold design and build, metal-to-plastic conversions, short-run production, mold transfer, and inventory management. Production volumes span from hundreds to millions of units annually.

The firm serves medical device OEMs as a UL-recognized, FDA-listed contract manufacturer, along with government research agencies and a broad base of Fortune 500 and regional industrial customers. Documented projects include feedthrough guides for government research and protocol studies for medical component materials.

Klann differentiates itself through in-house mold design and maintenance using SolidWorks, Master Unit Die (MUD) systems, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and a commitment to responsive service and long-term partnerships—principles rooted in its original pivot from organ building to plastics innovation.

name: Lewis Woodshop LLC
old_description: Lewis Woodshop is a custom woodshop located in rural Essex, Vermont that produces fine, heirloom-quality furniture. Using locally sourced materials, David builds each piece from hand, incorporating various styles, including Shaker, Japanese Kumiko and modern. Whether you want furniture that evokes the warmth and sophistication of Europe, the precision and architecture of Asuka-era Japan, or the rugged authenticity of Vermont, Lewis Woodshop has all your needs covered.
about:
Lewis Woodshop LLC operates from a 1,000-square-foot workshop in Essex, Vermont, a rural town about 20 minutes from Burlington. The business was founded by David Lewis, who grew up in Lutherville, Maryland, and developed a passion for fine furniture making while attending the Vermont Woodworking School. After completing his training, Lewis established his own shop, building each piece by hand using locally sourced, sustainably harvested lumber.

The shop produces custom furniture including tables, dressers, beds, chests, chairs, and decorative pieces such as Kumiko lanterns. Each item is crafted individually using a blend of power tools and traditional hand tools—chisels, saws, and sanders—allowing for both precision and artistic detail. The workshop spans roughly 1,000 square feet and is run solely by Lewis, who oversees every step from material selection to final finish.

Lewis Woodshop serves private clients seeking bespoke, heirloom-quality furniture for residential settings. Past commissions have included Shaker-style hall tables, Kumiko-adorned end tables and lanterns, pencil-post beds, and chests of drawers. The shop also collaborates with clients on one-of-a-kind designs, guiding them through wood selection, style, and design choices.

The company emphasizes a commitment to craftsmanship and sustainability. Lewis sources lumber that is sustainably grown and responsibly harvested, and he describes his work as a pursuit of harmony between utility and aesthetics, resulting in pieces that are considered functional works of art.

about:
Lexco Cable Manufacturing operates from Norridge, Illinois, where it has been a family-owned business since its founding in 1974. The company began as a manufacturer of wire rope, cable, and bungee cord assemblies, serving both standard and custom applications.

Today, Lexco fabricates custom wire rope assemblies, cable assemblies, bungee cord assemblies, push-pull controls, and architectural cable railings. Its capabilities include custom cut-to-length services, crimping, swaging, and engineering support, all backed by ISO 9001-certified quality processes. The shop handles small- to high-volume production with flexible order quantities and low minimums.

The company serves military, OEM, MRO, distributor, and contractor markets, as well as specialized sectors such as aerospace and defense, fitness, and agriculture. Customers include general contractors and aftermarket sellers who require load-rated termination solutions tailored to specific load capacities, environments, and installation methods.

Lexco differentiates itself by combining custom assembly fabrication with practical production support, offering quick turnarounds, application-specific engineering, and a CAGE code (1VXG5) for government contracting. Its 50-year track record reflects ongoing investment in people, processes, and capabilities.

name: Lima Sheet Metal
old_description: Family-owned and operated since 1974, serving Ohio with quality metal
about:
Lima Sheet Metal has operated from Lima, Ohio since 1974, when founder Michael Ray Emerick opened a shop to serve the local community with integrity and quality craftsmanship. The business remains family-owned and women-owned, now in its third generation under the leadership of CEO Anne Emerick, President James "Bo" Emerick, and General Manager Steve Emerick.

The company provides full-service sheet metal fabrication, structural steel work, ventilation and ductwork, and material handling equipment. Its in-house machine shop handles CNC and manual machining, MIG, TIG, and stick welding, press brake forming up to 12 feet, shearing, and plasma cutting. Capabilities extend to confined space entry services, on-site installation, and emergency welding repair, covering projects from custom prototypes to production runs.

Lima Sheet Metal serves industrial, commercial, and municipal clients throughout Ohio, with specialized expertise for the food and restaurant industries. Typical projects include custom guarding, drip pans, electrical enclosures, roofing and flashing, railing and stair systems, monorail and production line structures, canopy hoods, production carts, storage racks, and conveyors.

The founder's original vision — genuine care for every customer and hands-on quality — still drives the operation. The company emphasizes complete in-house control from design to installation, fast turnaround with quotes within 24 hours, and a safety-first approach backed by certified confined space technicians.

old_description: REMsafe SLEEP®, one of our family of businesses and a leading provider of sleep apnea solutions, has announced a new business relationship with TCW, a leading warehousing and distribution company. This relationship will provide offer TCW's fleet of 500 drivers with state-of-the-art sleep apnea treatment.
about:
Lincare is headquartered in Rolla, Missouri, and operates as a national provider of in-home respiratory care and durable medical equipment. The company delivers services directly to patients' homes as well as to nursing homes and long-term care facilities across the United States.

The company's core offerings span home oxygen therapy (stationary and portable), sleep apnea treatment with CPAP and bilevel PAP devices, nebulizer therapy for conditions such as COPD and asthma, and home INR testing for warfarin patients. Lincare also provides enteral nutrition support with trained dietitians, high-frequency chest wall oscillation therapy, powered mobility equipment including electric wheelchairs and scooters, pediatric respiratory services, pharmacy delivery, speech-generating devices, tracheostomy and suction management, and both invasive and non-invasive home ventilator care. Digital tools such as the VentCircle™ mobile app and a secure patient portal support supply ordering, usage tracking, and account management.

Lincare serves individuals with chronic respiratory conditions, sleep disorders, and mobility limitations, as well as institutional customers such as long-term care facilities. A noted business relationship includes providing sleep apnea treatment to the 500-driver fleet of warehousing and distribution company TCW through its REMsafe SLEEP® family of businesses. The company also supports Medicare beneficiaries and offers out-of-pocket options for services not covered by insurance.

Lincare states its mission is to set the standard for excellence in home respiratory care, aiming to enable patients with chronic conditions to remain engaged in life. Differentiators highlighted by the company include complimentary programs such as CareCheck™ for COPD early intervention, HeartSteps® for congestive heart failure management, and SleepEaze™ for sleep disorder education and adherence support.

old_description: Linear Fine Woodworking provides beautiful custom-built cabinetry and architectural millwork to areas like Phoenix and Scottsdale Arizona as well as the greater Southwest. Each Linear Fine Woodworking creation is a work of art crafted and custom-built just for you. Whether it’s custom designed kitchen cabinetry, a wall unit, home theatre unit, or office furniture, innovation in design and woodworking is a hallmark of Linear Fine Woodworking products.
about:
Linear Fine Woodworking operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where it has been designing and building custom cabinetry, furniture, and architectural millwork for more than three decades. The company serves clients across Phoenix, Scottsdale, and the broader Southwest region.

The shop produces custom cabinetry, architectural millwork, and furniture for residential and commercial projects. A distinctive capability is the in-house production of veneer panels from rough-cut flitches, a process that yields uniformly stable panels and expands design possibilities. The team works with exotic veneers, solid woods, glass, lighting, cabling, and specialized hardware to create pieces that blend function with sculpture.

Projects range from kitchen cabinetry and wall units to home theater installations and office furniture.

Linear Fine Woodworking emphasizes its combined team experience of over 350 years and its rare in-house veneer panel manufacturing as core differentiators. The firm was founded on the goal of merging custom furniture and cabinetry with fine art, a philosophy that continues to guide its approach.
